newsitem.title: USA: Philadelpha Electric rejects union - paper.
newsitem.headline: Philadelpha Electric rejects union - paper.

text.p: Philadelphia Electric (PECO) will remain the nation's largest non-union utility because employees voted against forming a bargaining unit, a newspaper reported on Saturday.

The company announced that 59 percent of 1,364 service employees rejected representation by the Utility Workers Union of America in balloting on Thursday, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported on Saturday. The vote results were announced late on Friday and will not be final until certified by the National Labor Relations Board.

It was the third representation vote won by PECO management, the newspaper said. Power generating employees rejected the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers in April, and nuclear plant staff rejected the UWUA in March.
"We believe that remaining union-free is in our best interest, the best interest of our employees and shareholders," said Corbin McNeill, chairman of PECO.
